```suggestion
			bezier_key_mode->set_tooltip_text(TTR("Bezier Default Mode\nSet the default handle mode of new Bezier keys."));
```
These should all be "Bézier" though for full correctness

We have weird cases on the Animation-side of things, where it is written as "bezier", while in all other places it's needed (e.g. Curve2D) it is correctly spelled. I can't tell if this is intentional because it seems to be quite consistent.

This probably needs an accessibility text too, doesn't it? Like, the first line of the tooltip, like @bruvzg seems to have done in other accessibility PRs.

You could be smart with this, and maybe use `String.get_slicec('\n', 0)` to obtain the accessibility text. Hmm...

This also could use a proper context in languages where gender matters (and not the only one by a large margin by the way)
For example, in French (and Italian) there's a difference between "La mode (feminine) inconnue" and "Le mode (masculine) inconnu". Although, French is particularly fortunate because the correct translation is masculine and suitably generic.

Changed to displaying the actual integer value when it's an unknown mode. So it'll be a line like this in the tooltip:

> Handle Mode: 42

The `default` branch are very unlikely to be executed and showing the value is more useful.
